Question: Let \(V\) be a 4-dimensional vector space and let \(G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,\operatorname{Sym}^2 V^\vee)\), so that a point of \(G\) is a 2-dimensional subspace \(W=\langle Q_0,Q_1\rangle\subset \operatorname{Sym}^2 V^\vee\), equivalently a pencil of quadrics in \(\mathbb P(V)\cong \mathbb P^3\). Let \(\operatorname{PGL}(V)\) act naturally on \(G\), and let \(U_{\mathrm{sm}}\subset G\) be the open locus of pencils whose complete intersection \(\{Q_0=Q_1=0\}\subset \mathbb P(V)\) is smooth. For such a pencil, its discriminant binary quartic is \(\Delta_W(s,t)=\det(sQ_0+tQ_1)\), which has a classical \(j\)-invariant on the smooth locus. Which of the following is the strongest existence statement valid in this setting?
Predicted label: 'C'
Predicted text: 'There exists a rational \\(\\operatorname{PGL}(V)\\)-invariant map \\(p\\colon G \\dashrightarrow \\mathbb P^1\\) whose restriction to \\(U_{\\mathrm{sm}}\\) is exactly the \\(j\\)-invariant of the discriminant binary quartic.'
Correct label: 'C'
Correct text: 'There exists a rational \\(\\operatorname{PGL}(V)\\)-invariant map \\(p\\colon G \\dashrightarrow \\mathbb P^1\\) whose restriction to \\(U_{\\mathrm{sm}}\\) is exactly the \\(j\\)-invariant of the discriminant binary quartic.'
Exact Match: 1.0
